1.explanation: The duplication stems from Dropdown.js passing a title prop to each ListBox.MenuItem (title={itemToString(item)}). That title attribute is rendered on the same element whose visible text is already the item label, causing VoiceOver to read it twice. Dropdown.js’s items.map callback is where title is injected, and ListBoxMenuItem simply forwards that title to the DOM. Removing or replacing the title attribute here (for example, using aria-label only or dropping it entirely) will eliminate the double announcement.
1.bug_scenario: When navigating the open Dropdown with VoiceOver on macOS, each option’s text is announced twice. For example, focusing “Option 4” yields: “Option 4” (inner text) and then again “Option 4” (from the title attribute), followed by the selected-count announcement (“selected (5 of 6)”). The attached screenshot shows VoiceOver reading the same label twice.

2.bug_scenario: When using VoiceOver on Mac to navigate through a Carbon React Dropdown, each list item is announced twice. VoiceOver reads the item text from the DOM node and then immediately reads the same text again from the element’s title attribute (and also reads the “selected (x of y)” state), causing a confusing duplicate announcement.
